correctness.rationale: The counterexample satisfies every hypothesis of Bhandari's Theorem 3.1: \(I=\{1\}\), both weighted subspaces are \(\mathbb R^2\) with weight \(1\), and both local systems are orthonormal bases with all bounds equal to \(1\). Fusion weaving has exact bound \(1\), while the admissible atomic weave \(\{f_{11},g_{12}\}=(e_1,e_1)\) has zero lower frame bound. For the surviving converse, atomwise weaving with bounds \(L,U\) applied to block-constant atomic subsets gives local energy \(Q_\sigma\); uniform local bounds give \(aE_\sigma\le Q_\sigma\le bE_\sigma\), hence fusion bounds \(L/b,U/a\).

value.rationale: The target is a published characterization intended to transfer weaving robustness between fusion frames and ordinary local frame systems. The failure occurs without pathological choices: one fusion block, unit weights, and two orthonormal local bases suffice. This shows that block-level switching cannot justify arbitrary atom-level switching and prevents the false implication from being used in applications or subsequent arguments. The surviving one-way implication and the prior blockwise theorem identify the exact safe replacement.
